# Climate Change Classroom Charts

A compact set of visuals for teaching how temperature anomaly and CO2 emissions changed from 2018 to 2023.

## Chart Data for Line, Bar, and Scatter Views

- **Line chart:** temperature anomaly over time
- **Bar chart:** annual CO2 emissions
- **Scatter plot:** CO2 emissions vs. temperature anomaly

Year-by-year data:
- 2018 — Temp anomaly: **0.82°C** | CO2: **36.7 Gt**
- 2019 — Temp anomaly: **0.95°C** | CO2: **36.8 Gt**
- 2020 — Temp anomaly: **1.02°C** | CO2: **34.8 Gt**
- 2021 — Temp anomaly: **0.86°C** | CO2: **36.3 Gt**
- 2022 — Temp anomaly: **0.89°C** | CO2: **37.1 Gt**
- 2023 — Temp anomaly: **1.18°C** | CO2: **37.4 Gt**

## Classroom Chart Set

### 1) Line Chart: Temperature Anomaly Over Time
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg

- X-axis: Year
- Y-axis: Temperature anomaly (°C)
- Pattern: overall upward trend with a small dip in 2021–2022
- Highest point: **2023 at 1.18°C**

### 2) Bar Chart: Annual CO2 Emissions
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/bar-chart.svg

- X-axis: Year
- Y-axis: CO2 emissions (Gt)
- Pattern: mostly stable around 36–37 Gt, with a drop in 2020
- Highest point: **2023 at 37.4 Gt**

### 3) Scatter Plot: CO2 Emissions vs. Temperature Anomaly
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/graph-up.svg

- X-axis: CO2 emissions (Gt)
- Y-axis: Temperature anomaly (°C)
- Pattern: weak short-term relationship in this small dataset
- Teaching point: climate trends are influenced by many factors, not just one year’s emissions

## Teaching Takeaways for High School Students

- **Global temperature is rising overall.** Even with small year-to-year changes, the long-term direction is upward.
- **CO2 emissions stayed high.** A single dip, like in 2020, did not change the overall trend for long.
- **Climate data needs context.** One year can be unusual, so scientists look at longer time periods.
- **Human activity matters.** Rising greenhouse gas emissions are a major driver of warming.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Build charts] https://www.chartgo.com/
Action: [Button: Learn climate basics] https://climate.nasa.gov/

## Sources

- NASA Climate: https://climate.nasa.gov/
- Our World in Data - CO2 and Greenhouse Gas Emissions: https://ourworldindata.org/co2-and-greenhouse-gas-emissions
- NOAA Climate Data: https://www.noaa.gov/climate
